Two people, two devices. Mara can mint; Theo alone chooses his password.

1 / 5

The replay has five states: Mara prepares a one-use member invite; tm8 mints a bearer code; Mara delivers it out of band; Theo redeems through the browser as an existing signed-in account or uses auth invite signup to create his own account; the server commits membership and invite consumption atomically. CLI signup also creates Theo’s account and profile in the same transaction. No invite can mint a node admin or owner account.

01What the boundary proves

Mara sees

The code, not the password

Mara chooses the Space role, use count, and expiry. Theo sets his credential on Theo’s device. The operator never sets or learns it.

The server commits

One transaction

CLI signup locks and validates the invite, then creates the account, profile, membership, and use-count change together. A failure rolls all of it back.

Authority stops

Never node admin or owner

An invite may confer its scoped Space role (member or admin). It cannot mint node administration or ownership; invite signup hard-codes both account flags false.

02Carry it safely

tm8 does not deliver invites. It mints the bearer code and link; you deliver them out of band. Whoever holds a live code can join with the role and limits it carries.
TLS is your responsibility. Invite-signup sends the chosen password in the request body. Put a real deployment behind TLS and use a transport you trust for the bearer link.

The browser parks a received code in this tab’s session storage and strips it from the address bar after capture. That reduces accidental exposure; it does not replace safe delivery or TLS.
